rationale: Greek loanword μεσότης 'mean, middle, mediation.' Aristotelian-philosophical term for the mediating position. Here describes the catechumen's purification as a 'mediation of agreement/truth' — a middle state between worldly defilement and elect purity. Standard Greek philosophical term.
Greek τροφή 'nourishment, food.' Standard term, paired here with οἰκονομία as the doublet of bodily-economic provisioning.
Greek οἰκονομία 'household-management, dispensation.' The administrative-providential order of the body's nourishment-arrangement.
Greek ἀντίδικος 'adversary at law' — already in glossary as ⲁⲛⲧⲓⲁⲕⲟⲥ. The Lyc. variant ⲁⲛⲧⲓⲁⲓⲕⲟⲥ shows ⲇⲓ → ⲁⲓ vowel-shift typical of this dialect.
Greek τάχα 'perhaps, maybe.' Standard adverbial particle; the catechumen's tentative formulation: 'perhaps the good I do shall not become sin.'
Lyc. ⲍⲁⲧⲉ = ϩⲟⲧⲉ 'fear' (regular ⲍ for ϩ). The ⲧⲣ̄- prefix forms an abstract 'state of fearing.' The catechumen's anxious admission: 'fear weighs heavy.'
Lyc. reflex of Greek ἐπειδή 'because, since.' Standard causal conjunction in dialectal form (with ⲡⲉⲓ- for ⲉⲡⲉⲓ-).

Tentative verbal form on the same root as ⲟⲩⲱⲃⲁ 'stripe/wound' (= ⲱϣⲃⲁ?). Final ⲁ may be perfect-3sg.f or part of a stem. The injury-context of the two-men parable strongly favors a wound-inflicting sense. Could alternatively be ⲟⲩⲱϣⲃ̄ 'answer' verbalized, but contextually less likely.
